210  THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

AFTER FIFTY YEARS

    We are making history here, today, in a reunion of old students of Savoy College, meeting for the first time fifty years after their old school has passed out of existence.

    The incorporated name of our old school was "The Savoy Male and Female College." It had elementary and college departments. The transition from the grades into the college department was no more than changing from one classroom into another. There was no such thing in those days as "going off to college." The college was right at home, and mother stayed at home too.

    I do not think that reunions were thought worthwhile, and certainly not practicable, until now, for several reasons. One reason is that students came from long distances to attend school, did not go home until the end of school, had little roads over which to travel in wagons and lighter vehicles with but little money to spare for the purpose. After graduation or leaving school, they scattered. It was difficult to get together for a reunion, as now with good roads, automobiles, and a better economic condition for all concerned.

    Another reason, I think, why our students made no effort at a reunion for fifty years, is that when Mr. Halsell moved away from Savoy and Texas, and there remained no nucleus about which to form such a reunion. So, the reunion spirit has been allowed to lie dormant for almost half a century. Happily, however, the grandchildren and great-grandchildren, as those of the old student body who are still living come together to show their respect for early struggles for an education, and live over in our memories the scenes, the experiences of those days in a school half a century ago. As I see this large gathering here it is a matter of significant historical interest, as I do not know about the life of the individual.

    In this reunion there is an outstanding difference to be noted in its purpose. There is no effort being made to evaluate or discover whether or not the Almighty involved as to the success or failure in life of the individual student, for the court of final review has already either made good or has not. For the most part the old students who have gathered around their old school have attained reasonable success in life.
notes: This is the text of the keynote address 'After Fifty Years' delivered by Gus W. Thomasson at the banquet.
